text:
Evan H: FYI: last night's global webinar caused ~60 leads to sit in 'pending-enrich' for >1h. Business SLA is 30m. Root cause looks like HS webhook retries plus SF connector throttling -> router stalls.
Marisol G: Oof. We should avoid long manual queues. Proposal: 'claim-graceback' - after 120s of pending enrichment mark as gracetime and perform a low-confidence assign to overflow-bot. If enrichment arrives later, allow one safe swap.
Ben T: Love the name. Keep scope narrow: only tag:webinar and sources [zoom, hopin], and exclude accounts with enterprise=true. Limit swaps=1.
Evan H: Also add metrics: grace_assigns, swap_count, duplicate_claims. Alert if duplicate_claims > 1 in 30m.
Ben T: Quick pseudo: ```
if (lead.tags.includes('webinar') && now - enrich.requested_at > 120000 && !lead.flags.grace_assigned) {
  lead.flags.grace_assigned = true;
  enqueueAssign(lead, 'overflow-bot', {confidence:'low', origin:'graceback'});
}
```
Marisol G: I'll draft the routing config and the short FAQ for Sales: owners with header X-Claim-Confidence=low are temporary.
Evan H: Can we canary this for 4h then roll back? Also ops-bot, please page #oncall on toggle.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled by Ben T at 2024-12-02T03:30:00Z for claim-graceback - watch #deploys
Ben T: PR: https://git.redwood/routing/pull/1476 - feature flag ff.claim_graceback true for canary. Tests passing.
Marisol G: I'll run replay with webinar set and simulate enrich delays. ETA 45m.
Evan H: Thanks team. If metrics look good, keep for weekend launch and then plan a permanent fix for the connector throttling.
